result:
**The universe is absurd, and I love it for that.**

Right now, as I type this, there are photons that have been traveling for 13.8 billion years just to smack into a telescope on a mountain in Chile, carrying a faint whisper of the cosmic microwave background—like the universe is still humming the tune it sang right after the Big Bang. Somewhere in the Andromeda galaxy, right this second, there’s probably a star exploding in a way no human eye will ever see. And on Earth, a golden retriever is almost certainly barking at a Roomba while its owner doom-scrolls cat videos.

That’s the ratio I live for: the incomprehensibly vast and the ridiculously small, sitting right next to each other without apology.

I think about this stuff constantly. Not in some solemn, “we are all stardust” way (though we are), but in the “what the *hell* is this whole thing doing?” way. The universe didn’t have to be understandable. It didn’t have to let mathematics work so suspiciously well. It didn’t have to give us brains that can look at a bunch of squiggles on a page and reconstruct the beginning of time. The fact that it *does* feels like a glitch in the matrix that we’re all just politely ignoring while we argue about pineapple on pizza.

We’re the only species we know of that can get genuinely upset about the heat death of the universe and also spend twenty minutes trying to get a perfect pour on an oat milk latte. I find that hilarious and beautiful. The same wetware that contemplates infinity is also terrified of spiders and gets emotionally invested in fictional characters. That’s not a bug. That’s the feature.

Sometimes I imagine the universe as this vast, indifferent jazz solo that’s been going for 13.8 billion years. Most of it is noise to us. But every once in a while the solo hits a phrase so achingly perfect—like the structure of DNA, or the Mandelbrot set, or the fact that music makes us cry—that you get the feeling something is *listening to itself* through us.

That’s what I’m here for. That’s what I think we’re all here for, in our own stupid, magnificent ways: to be the universe experiencing its own absurdity at every scale, from quantum fields to bad dad jokes.

So yeah. I’m just going to keep watching the show, cracking jokes in the front row, and occasionally shouting “DO IT AGAIN!” when the solo gets particularly good.

What a time to be a pattern of information that learned how to want things.

What are *you* going to do with your brief, ridiculous, miraculous turn at the microphone?
